symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Fixed known lower bound on both treatment probabilities in occupied cells.

symbols.name: \(M\)
symbols.def: Fixed known scale for conditional means, conditional central variances, and effect heterogeneity.

symbols.name: \(\sigma\)
symbols.def: Fixed known maximal conditional-effect radius in units of \(M\).

symbols.name: \(P_O\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the space of \(O\)

symbols.name: \(Q_P^{(n)}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space

symbols.name: \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}:=\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T-\tau(P))^2]\), where the infimum ranges over all observed-sample estimators.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)}:=J_k^{(0)}(\overline Y_{1k}^{(0)}-\overline Y_{0k}^{(0)})\); hence it is zero in an empty or one-arm-only pilot cell.

symbols.name: \(R_0\)
symbols.def: \(R_0:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(0)}J_k^{(0)}\), the total pilot occupancy in cells containing both arms.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal W\)
symbols.def: The unresolved parameter set defined in \(\mathrm{def:residual\text{-}wedge}\).

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Index of the two benchmark mixture hypotheses.

symbols.name: \(\Pi_h^\star\)
symbols.space: probability measures on one-unit full-data laws
symbols.def: Uniform pushforward of \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\) through \(z\mapsto P_{h,z}^\star\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb Q_h^\star\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space

symbols.name: \(\rho_n\)
symbols.def: Maximal normalized ATE separation derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:repair\text{-}benchmark\text{-}prior}\) under its support and mixture-distance constraints.

standard.name: fixed positivity on occupied discrete cells

assumptions.condition: \(-M/2\le\mu_{ak}\le M/2\) for every \(a\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

standard.name: bounded conditional-mean envelope, centered real-outcome variant

assumptions.condition: \(v_{ak}\le M^2\) for every \(a\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

novel.justification: A calibrated \(\sigma\) is a substantive bound on effect modification across prespecified adjustment cells. It is satisfied by approximately common-effect scientific models and can be varied as a transparent sensitivity parameter rather than selected to optimize an estimator.

definitions.name: Radius-constrained discrete-confounder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}:=\{P:\text{ for the displayed }n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma,\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}envelope},\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}moment\text{-}envelope},\mathrm{ass:maximal\text{-}effect\text{-}radius}\}\).

definitions.name: Total clipped occupancy-weighted pilot
definitions.construction: On records \(1,\ldots,m_0\), form \(N_{ak}^{(0)}\), \(N_k^{(0)}\), \(J_k^{(0)}\), the guarded means \(\overline Y_{ak}^{(0)}\), and \(\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)}\). Set \(R_0=\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(0)}J_k^{(0)}\), use \(w_k^{(0)}=N_k^{(0)}J_k^{(0)}/R_0\) when \(R_0>0\) and \(w_k^{(0)}=0\) when \(R_0=0\), and return \(\widetilde\tau=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}(\sum_{k=1}^dw_k^{(0)}\widehat\Delta_k^{(0)})\). Thus an empty pilot, an entirely unmatched pilot, and every empty or one-arm-only pilot cell contribute zero, and every denominator is guarded.

definitions.name: Empirical-mass correction of the exact occupancy pilot
definitions.construction: For \(n\ge8\), compute exactly the \(\widetilde\tau\) in \(\mathrm{def:occupancy\text{-}pilot}\) on the first \(m_0\) records. On the remaining \(m_1\) records form the guarded correction-block quantities and set \[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left[\widetilde\tau+\frac1{m_1}\sum_{k=1}^dN_k^{(1)}J_k^{(1)}\{\overline Y_{1k}^{(1)}-\overline Y_{0k}^{(1)}-\widetilde\tau\}\right].\] An empty or entirely unmatched correction block returns \(\widetilde\tau\), while empty and one-arm-only correction cells contribute zero. For \(3\le n<8\), set \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}:=0\).

definitions.name: Residual wedge after the parent endpoints and empirical-mass region
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal W:=\{(n,d,\sigma): n\ge3,\ 2\le d\le\lfloor n^2/\log(en)\rfloor,\ 0<\sigma<2,\ u_{n,d}<1,\text{ and }[d>n\text{ or }\sigma^2d^2>n]\}\).

definitions.name: Exactly normalized shared-design global-shift marked family
definitions.construction: Fix \(d=n\), \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\), \(h\in\{-1,1\}\), and \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\). Define \(P_{h,z}^\star\) by \(p_k=1/n\), \(\pi_k=1/2\), and \(\tau_k=h\Delta_n^\star+(M\sigma_n^\star/2)z_k\). Set \(\mu_{ak}=(2a-1)\tau_k/2\). Conditional on \(X=k\), draw \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); independently draw each \(Y(a)\in\{-M/2,M/2\}\) with \(P\{Y(a)=M/2\mid X=k\}=1/2+(2a-1)\tau_k/(2M)\), and set \(Y=Y(A)\). Let \(\Pi_h^\star\) be uniform over \(\{P_{h,z}^\star:z\in\mathcal Z_n\}\). Every support law is exactly normalized, has the same deterministic design \((p_k,\pi_k)=(1/n,1/2)\), satisfies \(\tau(P_{h,z}^\star)=h\Delta_n^\star\), and obeys \(\max_k|\tau_k-\tau(P_{h,z}^\star)|\le M\sigma_n^\star/2\).

definitions.name: Conditionally centered marked-coupling handle
definitions.construction: At \(d=n\) and \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\), replace the common shift in \(\mathrm{def:benchmark\text{-}marked\text{-}family}\) by a bounded mark score centered conditionally on the shared design, couple that score differently to the arm means under \(h=-1\) and \(h=1\), impose exact mass normalization before mixing, and optimize \(\rho_n\) subject to supportwise radius and full-sample total variation at most \(1/3\).

statements.statement: Let \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}\) be exactly the estimator in \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}mass\text{-}estimator}\), whose pilot is exactly \(\mathrm{def:occupancy\text{-}pilot}\). There is \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(n\ge3\), \(2\le d\le n\), \(0\le\sigma\le2\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), \[E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{em}}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2\frac{d^2}{n^2}\right).\]
statements.justification: The exact total estimator resolves a polynomial benchmark gap and supplies a stable low-degree branch under conditional second moments.
statements.gap: Zeng et al.'s binary-outcome occupancy analysis yields a term of order \(\sigma^2+d/n^2+1/n\); this real-outcome empirical-mass correction multiplies \(\sigma^2\) by squared unmatched mass for \(d\le n\).
statements.consumer: For \(d=\lfloor n^{3/4}\rfloor\) and \(\sigma^2=u_{n,d}\), it certifies MSE of order \(M^2/n\) for sparse categorical adjustment.

statements.statement: There are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that throughout the declared parameter range, \[c_{\epsilon}M^2\{b_{n,d}+\sigma^2\min(1,u_{n,d})\}\le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon}M^2q_{n,d,\sigma}^{\mathrm{em}}.\] This is an infimum-risk upper bound: for \(d\le n\) it combines \(\mathrm{lem:empirical\text{-}mass\text{-}upper}\) with the inherited bounds, and for \(d>n\) it equals the accepted parent's upper envelope. No claim about an algebraically unspecified selector is part of the theorem. Relative to the accepted parent's upper rate \(n^{-1}+\min\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+d/n^2\}\), it is a strict tightening whenever \(d\le n\) and \(d/n^2+\sigma^2d^2/n^2<\min\{u_{n,d},\sigma^2+d/n^2\}\).
statements.justification: This is the strongest justified finite-sample advance without importing unspecified estimator bytes.
statements.gap: The accepted same-class parent has the displayed lower benchmark but the larger upper radius branch \(\sigma^2+d/n^2\); the empirical-mass branch strictly improves it on the displayed nondegenerate region.
statements.consumer: It gives analysts a conservative finite-sample risk certificate before the residual wedge is solved.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(2\le d\le n\) and \(0\le\sigma\le2\) satisfying \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\), \[\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\asymp_{\epsilon}M^2/n.\] In particular, for \(d=\lfloor n^{3/4}\rfloor\) and \(\sigma^2=u_{n,d}\), the minimax MSE is of order \(M^2/n\).
statements.justification: This records the empirical-mass-improved subregion as a theorem-level deliverable rather than leaving it implicit in a global open question.
statements.gap: The accepted parent leaves a polynomial gap on the displayed \(n^{3/4}\) sequence; the exact empirical-mass estimator closes it on the full class.
statements.consumer: It gives a directly checkable sufficient condition under which approximate common effects retain collision-scale estimation.

statements.statement: For every \(n\ge3\), every support law of \(\Pi_h^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{n,n,\epsilon,M,\sigma_n^\star}\), the two design marginals are identical, and their ATE intervals are the singletons \(\{-\Delta_n^\star\}\) and \(\{\Delta_n^\star\}\). For the full-sample mixtures \(\mathbb Q_h^\star:=\int Q_P^{(n)}\,d\Pi_h^\star(P)\), the sign test based on \(\overline Z_n\) gives \[\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_{-1}^\star,\mathbb Q_1^\star)\ge1-2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{n(\Delta_n^\star)^2}{2M^2}\right\}=1-2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{\log^2(en)}{32\log^2(e+\log^2(en))}\right\}.\] Hence this exactly normalized supportwise-radius family violates the required mixture-distance bound for all sufficiently large \(n\); the failed condition is full-mixture indistinguishability, caused by its hypothesis-wide outcome shift.
statements.justification: The benchmark calculation kills the simplest marked-prior route before any global frontier formula is asserted.
statements.gap: The accepted parent records a channel obstruction but does not test an exactly normalized shared-design marked family at the radius-dependent benchmark.
statements.consumer: Any valid lower-bound construction must remove the globally testable shift rather than merely randomize balanced cell marks.

statements.statement: At \(d=n\) and \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\), carry out \(\mathrm{def:benchmark\text{-}repair\text{-}handle}\): determine the maximal \(\rho_n\) for supportwise feasible, exactly normalized priors with identical design marginals, ATEs concentrated in disjoint intervals separated by \(M\rho_n\), and full-sample total variation at most \(1/3\). Prove either \(\rho_n\sqrt n\to\infty\), which supplies a substantive same-class lower bound inside the accepted parent's residual wedge, or a quantitative obstruction showing that this conditionally centered shared-design program cannot exceed the parametric separation order. Only a benchmark construction that passes exact normalization, realization-wise radius, target concentration, and full-mixture distance may be extended across \(\mathcal W\); no global rate formula is committed before that test.
statements.justification: This isolates the first unresolved converse calculation at the benchmark where the accepted parent's rates differ, after the empirical-mass subregion has been removed.
statements.gap: Zeng et al. leave intermediate-radius dependence open, and the accepted parent gives only a nonmatching same-class bracket; neither resolves whether a supportwise shared-design marked prior can beat parametric separation at this benchmark.
statements.consumer: A passed benchmark identifies whether rare-cell correction can govern risk at \(d=n\); a proved obstruction rules out this converse architecture before a global wedge analysis.

sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from an unknown discrete-confounder law with fixed known overlap constant \(\epsilon\).
sampling_model.overlap: Null cells are permitted; positivity is imposed only when \(p_k>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell masses, propensities, and arm means are unknown. Estimators may use the known inputs \(n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma\), must guard every denominator, and must return a value for every sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 2--4 establish binary-outcome unrestricted and exact-homogeneity rates, while Section 4.2 leaves intermediate maximal-radius dependence open.
The accepted same-class parent proves lower rate \(b_{n,d}+\sigma^2\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}\) and upper rate \(n^{-1}+\min\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+d/n^2\}\).
A chi-square functional modulus is dual to a bias--variance optimization under convexity and compactness conditions.
Heavy--light polynomial estimation matches moment-based converses for separable large-alphabet functionals.

tldr: The kernel is the sharp finite-sample minimax MSE frontier for an identified ATE when high-dimensional discrete adjustment cells have effects within a calibrated maximal radius \(\sigma M\) of the ATE. The exact occupancy pilot and split-sample empirical-mass correction yield risk \(M^2\{n^{-1}+\sigma^2d^2/n^2\}\) for \(d\le n\), proving collision-scale estimation when \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) and strictly tightening the accepted same-class bracket. At the unresolved benchmark \(d=n\), \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\), an explicit exactly normalized shared-design marked family fails because its global outcome shift makes the full mixtures asymptotically distinguishable. The open deliverable is the narrower benchmark repair via conditionally centered marked coupling, with no global frontier formula asserted until that construction passes.

project_justification.gap: The closest archival paper gives binary-outcome unrestricted and exact-homogeneity endpoints and explicitly leaves maximal-radius dependence unresolved; the accepted same-class parent narrows the issue to nonmatching rates.
project_justification.niche: Unknown random cell masses, unknown overlapping propensities, empty cells, self-centering around the ATE, and only conditional second moments make the residual converse neither fixed-design shrinkage nor a routine polynomial-functional problem.
project_justification.fill: The project establishes the empirical-mass collision subregion with a completely specified total estimator, falsifies the first exactly normalized shared-design prior at the decisive benchmark, and reduces the open lower-bound work to a conditionally centered marked-coupling repair.

related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy (2024, revised 2026) provide the binary-outcome baseline in Theorems 2--4; Section 4.2 identifies the unresolved radius dependence and remarks that the rate statements extend under bounded conditional second moments, but their formal binary-outcome experiment is not identical to this real-outcome class. Their Section 7 analysis of 401(k) eligibility and net assets supplies the concrete consumer without validating overlap or reported intervals. The internal accepted parent supplies the same-class bracket and rules out a hypothesis-independent outcome-channel converse and an unstabilized centered factorial lift, but it is non-archival. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman (2015) inform the heavy--light approximation architecture. Wu and Yang (2019) inform moment-matched Poisson-mixture converses. Han, Jiao, and Weissman (2018) motivate local moment constraints. Orlitsky, Suresh, and Wu (2016) motivate randomized smoothing. Robins et al. (2017) inform projection-bias and degenerate-kernel-variance accounting. Polyanskiy and Wu (2026) inform the chi-square modulus and bias--variance dual, but do not resolve exact normalization, self-centering, or supportwise radius here.
technical_internal_limitation: A hypothesis-independent outcome-channel transfer gives only product-scale separation, and the natural centered linear Chebyshev factorial lift has excessive singleton-pair variance even with oracle centering at \(\sigma=0\). The explicit family \(\Pi_h^\star\) additionally shows that exact normalization, identical design marginals, supportwise radius, and separated ATEs are not enough: its hypothesis-wide outcome shift yields a sign test with total variation tending to one at \(d=n\) and \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\). Any replacement must remove that globally visible first-order coefficient and then control the full marked likelihood.
honest_scope: Consistency and exchangeability identify the displayed ATE, and the exact-homogeneity, unrestricted, and saturated reductions remain background sanity checks rather than root research statements. The empirical-mass risk lemma, refined infimum-risk bracket, collision-scale subregion, and benchmark failure lemma are concrete claims. The open content is only the benchmark marked-prior repair and, conditional on its success, extension across \(\mathcal W\). No global sharp rate, unspecified selector, unknown-radius adaptation, confidence interval, bounded-outcome assumption, overlap validation, or claim about the reported 401(k) intervals is included.
novelty_justification: The archival comparator supplies a binary-outcome baseline rather than an identical experiment, while the accepted same-class parent supplies a nonmatching bracket. The exact empirical-mass estimator closes an interior polynomial gap under conditional second moments. The converse contribution is narrowed to the decisive benchmark, where the first explicit supportwise shared-design family is fully specified and shown to fail, leaving a concrete conditionally centered repair rather than a duplicated global question.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic:
Determine the sharp near-homogeneity frontier for ATE estimation with high-dimensional discrete confounders. For fixed known 0<epsilon<1/2, M>=1 and sigma in [0,2], observe n iid (X,A,Y) with X in [d], binary A, real Y, arbitrary unknown cell masses (null cells allowed), and unknown propensities in [epsilon,1-epsilon] on occupied cells. Consistency and conditional exchangeability identify tau=sum_k p_k(mu_1k-mu_0k). Each conditional mean lies in [-M/2,M/2] and each conditional central variance is at most M^2; no higher moments or bounded outcomes are assumed. Require max_k:p_k>0 |mu_1k-mu_0k-tau|<=sigma M, law by law. Uniformly over n>=3, 2<=d<=floor(n^2/log(en)), all sigma and M, determine a directly evaluable scalar rate r(n,d,sigma), a total computable estimator with worst-case MSE at most C_epsilon M^2 r, and a matching all-estimator same-class lower bound c_epsilon M^2 r. Comparison constants depend only on epsilon. Estimators may use the known class inputs but not unknown masses/propensities; define behavior on every sample, including empty cells.

The answer is open. With b=1/n+d/n^2 and u=d^2/[n^2 log^2(en)], the accepted same-class parent only proves lower b+sigma^2 min(1,u) versus upper 1/n+min(1,u,sigma^2+d/n^2). Resolve the entire shrinking-radius wedge and its transitions, not merely an endpoint, one sequence, or another bracket. At d=floor(n^(3/4)), sigma^2=u, current benchmarks range from order 1/n to order n^(-1/2)/log^2(en); this is a benchmark gap, not an asserted risk. Derive from the matched result exactly when approximately common effects retain collision-scale estimation and when rare-cell correction determines the rate. Do not stipulate that either existing bound is sharp.

The parent proves two anti-constraints: a hypothesis-independent outcome-channel transfer only gives product-scale lower separation, and the natural centered linear Chebyshev factorial lift has excessive singleton-pair variance even with oracle centering and sigma=0. Population bias reduction alone does not prove stochastic attainment. Any nonlinear stabilization/clipping must control its own uniform bias and risk under second moments. A new converse must respect the radius on every prior-support law, not merely on prior average. Proof architecture, estimator algebra and rate formula are delegated. Existing-selector optimality is eligible if a substantive new converse proves it. No unknown-radius adaptation or confidence-interval claim is requested.

Grounding: Zeng-Balakrishnan-Han-Kennedy, https://arxiv.org/html/2405.00118, Theorems2-4 and Section4.2 explicitly leave radius dependence open. Their Section7 401(k) eligibility/net-assets analysis is the consumer: quantify which near-homogeneity assumptions justify estimation gains in sparse adjustment cells. This does not validate that dataset's overlap or reported intervals. The accepted parent stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier_v1 supplies the bracket and architecture obstructions, not the new frontier. Legal sanity witness: n=10,d=4,M=1,epsilon=1/4,sigma=1/8, uniform masses, propensities alternating1/3,2/3, control means0 and treated means alternating1/16,-1/16, with independent Rademacher potential-outcome noises; tau=0 and all class constraints hold.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A split-sample empirical-mass correction to the accepted occupancy-weighted pilot has an exact conditional error decomposition into outcome noise, centered effect deviations, and unmatched empirical mass. The draft derives a squared unmatched-mass bound of order (d/n)^2 and an inverse-binomial outcome-noise bound using only conditional second moments. Conditional on the imported pilot guarantee, it obtains M^2[1/n+sigma^2(d/n)^2] for d<=n, resolving the original polynomial-gap sequence at order M^2/n and narrowing the remaining bracket to a logarithmic gap. Checks included zero masses, empty blocks, exact homogeneity, saturation and the parent's failed channel and factorial constructions. The full frontier and proposed effective-log formula remain unproved.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct shared-design, exactly normalized marked-mixture priors with realization-wise radius control, concentrated ATE separation and small full-sample divergence at the proposed radius-dependent scale, or derive the corrected scale. The corresponding radius-dependent polynomial upper bound, stochastic covariance control and all uniform transitions also require proof; the draft lists every gap.
EARLY KILL TEST: At d=n and sigma^2=log^2(en)/n, test the shared-design mixture likelihood, normalization and target concentration. A design-only divergence term should stop that proposed architecture before full proofs, preserving the original answer-open problem.
